statements.t: "The external headwinds we faced in the second quarter — market dynamics, project delays and higher fuel costs — carried into the third.
We're targeting more third-party materials sales, right-sizing crews and equipment where market conditions call for it, and pursuing more private-work opportunities.

Our EDGE efforts have contributed to EBITDA growth and Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion, and while these efforts will continue, we have begun implementing ‘Sharper EDGE’ initiatives to drive additional value.
We look forward to discussing the details of Sharper EDGE at an investor day in the coming months.

For the remainder of 2026, the company expects to spend $55.4 million on organic growth projects.
Approximately 82% of the company's contracting services backlog relates to publicly funded projects, including street and highway construction projects.

We serve both public and private markets, with public projects making up most of our work and providing stability through economic cycles, which helps offset the cyclical nature of the private markets.

Federal and state funding remain at or near record levels for a majority of our markets with approximately 80 percent of our historical contracting services revenue each year coming from public-sector projects, enhancing stability through market cycles.
Of the $857 million of backlog at September 30, 2026, we expect to complete approximately $691 million in the 12 months following September 30, 2026.

Approximately 82 percent of our backlog at September 30, 2026, is related to publicly funded projects, including street and highway construction projects, which are driven primarily by public works projects for state departments of transportation (DOT).
It is estimated that a total of $2.2 trillion in funding will be needed for our roadway systems to reach a state of good repair during that time period.
In 2023, we launched our EDGE initiatives and established specialized teams to deliver training, support higher-margin bidding opportunities across regions and pursue targeted growth opportunities.

Building on the progress of these initiatives, which continue, we launched Sharper EDGE, a program of targeted improvement opportunities across three areas: Operational Excellence, Commercial Excellence and Organizational Excellence.
We have begun implementing these initiatives and expect to ramp the program over the next three years.

We are experiencing competitive market dynamics, primarily within contracting services, which is resulting in projects being more competitively bid and in turn compressing our contracting services margins.
We will continue to monitor the effects these economic conditions have on our business.
Pursuing our strategic growth goals through targeted acquisitions is expected to drive an increase in selling, general and administrative expenses on a year-over-year basis.
Our management team continues to evaluate growth opportunities, both through organic growth and acquisitions they believe will generate shareholder value.

Our business development team is focused on our growth with materials-led businesses in mid-size, higher growth markets, and has several targets at various stages of completion in our acquisition pipeline.
In addition, we continue to invest in multiple organic projects, including an aggregate expansion project in South Dakota and ready-mix operations in Idaho, Minnesota and Texas.
The aggregate expansion project will increase our production capabilities in the Sioux Falls market and is scheduled to be operational in 2027.

As of September 30, 2026, we had sufficient liquid assets and borrowing capacity to meet our financial commitments, debt obligations and anticipated capital expenditures for at least the next 12 months.

Our principal uses of cash in the future will be to fund our operations, working capital needs, capital expenditures, repayment of debt, organic growth and strategic business development transactions.

Additionally, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we spent $266.7 million on growth initiatives, which consisted of $185.7 million on acquisitions and $81.0 million on aggregate expansion and greenfield projects.
For the remainder of 2026, we estimate spending of $55.4 million on organic growth projects.
A large portion of the surety bonds are expected to expire within the next 12 months; however, we will likely continue to enter into surety bonds for our subsidiaries in the future.
We expect the termination process to extend through 2028 and include participant elections, regulatory filings, and the purchase of annuity contracts for certain participants.
Upon completion of the settlement transactions, we expect to recognize previously unrecognized actuarial losses currently included in accumulated other comprehensive loss.
We do not expect to make any pension plan contributions in 2026 as the plans are fully funded.
